english.title: Send false communication with intent to cause harm
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, sent a message conveying information you knew to be false, intending, at the time of sending it, the message, or the information in it, to cause non-trivial psychological or physical harm to a likely audience
english.legislation: Contrary to section 179 of the Online Safety Act 2023.

english.notes:
(i) From the 31st January 2024, this offence replaces that under section 1(1)(a)(iii) of the Malicious Communications Act 1988 (see H12181 - send letter / communication / article conveying false information) and that under section 127(2)(a) and (b) of the Communications Act 2003 (see H5557 - send false message by public electronic communication network to cause annoyance, inconvenience or anxiety, and causing such a message to be sent, H5558).
(ii) See section 179(7) and (8) of the Online Safety Act 2023 providing an extended prosecuting time limit for this offence.
(iii) Section 185 of that Act provides extra-territorial application and jurisdiction for certain offences under Part 10 of the Act, including that under section 179(1).
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), the defendant, without reasonable excuse, sent a message conveying information knowing it to be false, intending, at the time of sending it, the message, or the information in it, to cause non-trivial psychological or physical harm to a likely audience.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty depends on the maximum term for summary offences, see section 179(5) and (6) of the Online Safety Act 2023; for offences committed before section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes into force, this is 6 months, for offences committed after that time 51 weeks.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 179(7) and (8).
